extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale, and a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering.
extraction.license: Permissive open-source licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1)
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected using a scalable, fully automated pipeline for continuous collection of software engineering tasks from real-world GitHub repositories. The process involves four stages: preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and cloned repositories, automated installation instruction configuration using LLMs, execution-based installation verification in containers, and automated instance quality assessment using a fine-tuned LLM.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GitHub Archive (public events, issues, pull requests) and cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025 were used for the initial dataset construction.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Pull requests were linked to issues. Patches were divided into solution patches (non-test files) and test patches (test files). Tasks were grouped by project versions inferred from git tags. Installation recipes were generated and refined by LLMs. Dependency versions were frozen after successful setup.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering criteria included: Python repository with permissive license, resolved issue, merged PR, PR not linked to multiple issues, issue description > 10 characters, PR introduces/modifies tests, changes affect 1-15 files. Execution-based verification ensured tests failed before the patch and passed after. Automated quality assessment filtered for issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Quality labels (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness) were generated by fine-tuning Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified. Each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy for Task Complexity, 67% for Test Patch Correctness, and 79% for Issue Clarity on the validation set. These labels are provided as metadata to allow users to filter tasks.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and benchmark are continuously updated with fresh tasks. The leaderboard is publicly accessible and updated regularly. The maintainers are the authors from Nebius.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to accelerate open-source research and improve the reliability of LLM-based software engineering agents. Potential risks include overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors advocate for openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking to mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited exclusively to Python projects in the initial release, restricting applicability to other language ecosystems. The automated quality assessment may contain errors and decrease quality compared to human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable. The LLM-based approach for installation instructions was validated on a limited set of repositories. The dataset is limited to Python. The automated quality assessment is not perfect and may not replicate nuanced human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training (specifically reinforcement learning) and evaluation (benchmarking) of LLM-based software engineering agents.
